title: Glossary
text: Terms used across the Manifold course. Runtime vocabulary aligns with the Phase 7 constructive-realization contract. For Pico-side vocabulary (Rule, Parser, Composer, Pico), see the Pico course glossary. For composition vocabulary (XRD, Composition, XR, Managed Resource), see the Crossplane course glossary.

title: Glossary
text:
Channel
A named runtime pathway that carries typed values between Elements inside an InteractionTopology. In this course, one Wrangler-declared Channel wires exactly one event into the hosted Pico. The Channel is the wire; it is not the payload.

title: Glossary
text:
Control Surface
An operator- or learner-facing interface that expresses OperatorIntent against declared runtime state. In this course the Control Surface is a small Python CLI-style shell command (kubectl exec / curl) that sends one event onto the Channel. Graphical Control Surfaces (for example, Home Assistant) are out of scope.

title: Glossary
text:
Event
A single value delivered onto a Channel. Under the Phase 7 contract an event conforms to an EventType — described here in prose and a small inline shape rather than a formal schema.

title: Glossary
text:
EventType
The typed contract for values carried by a Channel. In this course the only EventType is hello.request, a small JSON-shaped payload carrying a value field that the hosted Pico echoes back on its log.

title: Glossary
text:
InteractionTopology
A declarative description of which Elements interact through which Channels within a RuntimeEnvironment. In this course the topology is minimal: one Pico and one Channel, authored as a small Wrangler-style YAML fragment shipped with the lab.

title: Glossary
text:
Manifold
The RuntimeEnvironment taught in this course. Manifold hosts Pico Elements on a Kubernetes RuntimeSubstrate and owns their lifecycle and notification path. Manifold does not replace Kubernetes, Crossplane, or Sandcastle — it sits on top of them.

title: Glossary
text:
Observation
A runtime-captured fact about an Element’s behaviour inside a RuntimeEnvironment. In this course the single Observation is the one log line the hosted Pico prints in response to the one event sent onto its Channel. Observations feed Phase 2 feedback[].

title: Glossary
text:
OperatorIntent
A declaration of desired runtime state expressed through a Control Surface. In this course the OperatorIntent is: “send one hello.request event to the hosted Pico via channel hello, and capture the response.”

title: Glossary
text:
Pico engine
The in-process host, inside Manifold, that actually runs a Pico Element. The Pico engine consumes events from a Channel and produces Observations. It is the runtime counterpart of the hello-world-pico artifact produced by the Hello Pico lab.

title: Glossary
text:
RuntimeEnvironment
A concrete environment hosted on the RuntimeSubstrate in which Pico Elements execute and interact. In this course the RuntimeEnvironment is Manifold, deployed onto a local minikube cluster. A RuntimeEnvironment runs on the RuntimeSubstrate; it does not replace it.

title: Glossary
text:
RuntimeSubstrate
The underlying execution layer that hosts every runtime Element in the academy. In this course, and across the Hello Pico roadmap, the RuntimeSubstrate is always Kubernetes (concretely, minikube).

title: Glossary
text:
Wrangler
The InteractionTopology authoring surface. Wrangler outputs a declarative topology (Channels, subscriptions, children) that Manifold applies over the runtime. Wrangler is not the runtime; it is an additional declarative input to the same Realization chain.

title: Manifold
text: Welcome to Manifold, the first runtime-focused course of the Open Engineering Academy. This course frames the smallest honest runtime story for a single Pico: one Pico Element, hosted by Manifold on a local Kubernetes cluster, wired through one Wrangler-declared Channel, receiving one event and producing one observable response.

title: Manifold
text:
Where this course fits
Manifold is a runtime course, not a fourth phase alongside compose / construct / behave. The three-layer story still holds:

Crossplane composes, Sandcastle constructs, Picos behave.

Manifold names the runtime host on which behaviour is observed. Under the Phase 7 constructive-realization contract, the role assignments this course teaches are:







Tool
Runtime role




Kubernetes
RuntimeSubstrate — the underlying execution layer


Manifold
RuntimeEnvironment — Kubernetes-hosted host for Pico Elements


Pico engine
The in-process host inside Manifold that runs Pico Elements


Wrangler
InteractionTopology authoring — declares Channels and subscriptions


Crossplane
Realization step — composes runtime resources onto the substrate


Sandcastle
Realization step — constructs the executable form of a Pico









ImportantScope — one Pico, one event, one response



This course keeps the runtime story narrow on purpose. It covers one Pico, hosted by one Manifold RuntimeEnvironment, wired through one Wrangler Channel, receiving one event and producing one observable response. Multi-Pico topologies, fleet orchestration, graphical control surfaces (for example, Home Assistant), and non-Kubernetes runtimes are explicitly out of scope for this first runtime course.

title: Manifold
text:
What you will learn
By the end of the course you will be able to:

Describe what a RuntimeSubstrate, a RuntimeEnvironment, an InteractionTopology, a Channel, an EventType, and an Observation are, using the Phase 7 vocabulary.
Explain how a Pico Element produced by the Hello Pico lab is hosted by a Manifold RuntimeEnvironment without being replaced by it.
Explain how a Wrangler-declared Channel wires exactly one event into the hosted Pico and how the resulting response is observed.
Run the accompanying Hello Pico on Manifold lab end-to-end on a local minikube cluster and capture the single observed response as the lab’s produced artifact.

See the course descriptor in metadata.yaml for the machine-readable summary (id, level, duration, prerequisites, runtime_substrate, runs_on).

title: Manifold
text:
Prerequisites

Completion of the Pico course, or equivalent familiarity with Rules, the Parser, the Composer, and the hello-world-pico artifact.
Completion of the Kubernetes setup foundation so docker, minikube, and kubectl resolve on your PATH.
Familiarity with the Crossplane course and the Hello Pico on Kubernetes lab is helpful but not required; this course consumes their outputs rather than replaces them.

title: Manifold
text:
How this course is structured
This first runtime course is intentionally small: an overview page (this file), a shared glossary, and one runnable lab. It does not yet carry a Part 1 / Part 2 / Part 3 structure — the runtime story is scoped to a single Pico so that later curriculum waves can extend it without retrofitting.
courses/manifold/
  _quarto.yml          # this course website
  index.qmd            # you are here
  metadata.yaml        # machine-readable course descriptor
  glossary.qmd         # course glossary
The runnable material lives in the reusable lab:

Hello Pico on Manifold lab — deploy a Manifold RuntimeEnvironment onto a local minikube cluster, host a single Pico inside it via a Wrangler-declared Channel, send one event, and observe one response.

title: Manifold
text:
What you will produce
A single artifact directory named hello-world-pico-on-manifold — the lab captures the exact manifests applied to the cluster, the Wrangler channel spec, the one event sent in, and the one observed response line printed by the hosted Pico. This matches the produces entry in metadata.yaml.

title: Manifold
text:
Start here

Hello Pico on Manifold lab — the single runnable path for this course.
Hello Two Picos lab — the first multi-Pico runtime lab that builds directly on Hello Pico on Manifold. It reuses the same Manifold RuntimeEnvironment on Kubernetes and adds a second named Pico plus one Wrangler-declared producer→consumer wiring. Run it after Hello Pico on Manifold when you are ready for the smallest honest two-Pico interaction.
